finding: The canonical snapshot defines an explicit privacy boundary, but the film does not make that boundary visible to the viewer. The scene visibly labels the snapshot as READ-ONLY and task parcels as source-bound, while the only statement about hidden reasoning is a code comment rather than rendered evidence. A viewer can see identifiers, status, and aggregate counts without being told which fields are allowed or which sensitive fields are excluded.

candidate_change.scope: candidate only; do not modify production files
candidate_change.change: Add a fixed-in-frame, source-derived privacy boundary card during the data reveal and keep it legible through the receipt beat. Render two compact lines: SHOWN: agent id / model family / status / restart count / aggregate counts; NOT SHOWN: encrypted reasoning / raw thoughts / credentials / environment secrets / prompt content. Build the labels from source['privacy'] so the visual contract cannot drift from the canonical source.
candidate_change.intended_effect: Make the read-only boundary explicit at the moment the worker traces and aggregate task parcels are visible, without adding any forbidden data or changing the underlying snapshot.

evidence.observation: The source has five allowed categories (agent id, model family, status, restart count, aggregate counts) and five forbidden categories (encrypted reasoning, raw thoughts, credentials, environment secrets, prompt content).

The scene renders a READ-ONLY snapshot stamp, agent labels, working/idle/task aggregates, source-bound task text, RECEIPT, and a place/not-chat footer; it does not render the canonical allowed/forbidden lists.
The phrase 'no hidden reasoning' exists only in a source comment, so it is not viewer-visible QA evidence.

ffprobe measured an H.264 render at 854x480, 15 fps, 172 frames, 11.466016 seconds. A sampled late frame visibly contains READ-ONLY, source-bound/no fabricated geometry, aggregate counts, WORLD, RECEIPT, and the footer, but no privacy allow/forbid card. The user-supplied showcase/films/WorldBoundAgentsV1.mp4 path is absent; this actual render path was used for the sample.

falsifier: The finding is false if a candidate render, independently sampled at start, midpoint, and receipt/end frames, contains a persistent, legible privacy boundary card that covers every canonical allowed and forbidden category and does not expose any forbidden field elsewhere in the frame.
